# Inverse Hyperbolic Secant

![Inverse Hyperbolic Secant function icon](../../../../assets/function-icons/functions/math/hyperbolic/10_Asech.svg)

[Mathematics functions](../../mathematics/index.md) · [All functions](../../index.md)

Returns the non-negative real y such that sech(y)=x, or the principal complex result. Input x; output arcsech. Finite real domain 0&lt;x≤1. asech(1)=+0; FROG defines asech(+0)=+Infinity and asech(−0)=NaN. Negative x and x&gt;1 give NaN. Example: Asech(0.8) = ln(2).

## Types and Compatibility

The notes below retain the reviewed help's original NI and Studio scopes. An NI overload is not a claim of Studio runtime support; the authoring profile and execution limits remain separate.

<details>
<summary>Retained binding and help statements</summary>

These are source declarations, not the current measured product-execution assessment. Compare historical limitations with the separately dated native profiles above.

Numeric scalar, array or numeric-only cluster; integer leaves produce F64 and floating-point precision is retained. Complex inverses use principal branches; non-finite complex results are unavailable. NaN propagates; real domain errors produce NaN without changing the output to complex. No angle conversion. Local Highlight calculation is available.

F32/F64 and finite C32/C64 inputs retain their precision; integer leaves convert to F64 before calculation and values above 2^53 may round. Arrays are processed element by element, preserving rank and dimensions; recursively numeric clusters preserve ordered fields. Typed empty arrays remain typed. String, Boolean, reference, mixed nonnumeric clusters, fixed-point, extended precision and Matrix inputs are not supported. The input x is required; the F64 unwired preview is not a numerical default. Local Highlight calculation uses frog.studio.hyperbolic.asech. Real NaN propagates; real inputs never become complex based on their value. Principal complex branches are used; non-finite complex results fail with a capability diagnostic.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Notes de types et de compatibilité de l’aide Studio</summary>

Les mentions NI et Studio gardent leur portée d’origine. Une variante NI ne constitue pas une déclaration de prise en charge par le runtime Studio ; consultez les profils et limites d’exécution de cette fiche.

Scalaire, tableau ou cluster entièrement numérique ; les entiers produisent du F64 et la précision flottante est conservée. Les inverses complexes utilisent les branches principales ; les résultats complexes non finis sont indisponibles. NaN se propage ; un réel hors domaine produit NaN sans devenir complexe. Aucune conversion d’angle. Le calcul local Highlight est disponible.

</details>
